notes: GPUI PANEL. The target UI framework is GPUI 0.2.2 (Zed's framework), not React. You have no training knowledge of this exact API, so read before writing: rever/src/main.rs (the app shell: how views, listeners, hover, scrolling, text fields and theme are used here), every file in rever-ui-kit/src (theme tokens, icons, strings via `Lang::t`, the TextInput entity, preview::run), vendor/gpui/examples/*.rs (uniform_list.rs, scrollable.rs, input.rs) and vendor/gpui/src/elements/*.rs for exact method names. What to build: two view structs implementing gpui::Render that reproduce the React components' layout, sizes, colors and behaviors (level filters, clear, expanding an entry, stack traces). Colors and sizes come from src/renderer/src/styles.css tokens (already in rever_ui_kit::theme::Theme; if a token is missing, define it locally and list it in your report). Data: the React code reads console entries and exceptions over IPC; here the views take `Arc<Mutex<rever_core::traffic::TrafficStore>>` (it holds the console and exception logs; read rever-core/src/traffic.rs for the API) plus a `refresh` method the host calls when something new arrives. Message formatting is already ported in rever-formats (console_format); use it as a path dependency. All user-facing strings go through `rever_ui_kit::i18n::Lang::t(key)` with the same keys the TSX uses. Keep logic (filtering, formatting) in plain functions with Korean-named unit tests; a .tsx file gets the `Port of` marker only when its behaviors are all there. Preview: fill examples/preview.rs so `cargo run -p rever-ui-console --example preview_console` shows both views with realistic fixture data (use rever_ui_kit::preview::run). Look at your own work: while it runs, `scripts/capture-window.sh preview_console /tmp/preview_console.png` captures only that window; read the PNG, compare with what the TSX would render, fix what is off. Do not bring windows to the front, do not capture the screen any other way, and do not run the `rever` app. The first build of a GPUI crate takes a few minutes.
